newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indocement begins work on $230 mln plant.
newsitem.headline: Indocement begins work on $230 mln plant.

text.p: Indonesian cement maker PT Indocement Tunggal Prakarsa started building a new $230 million plant on Friday at its complex in West Java, a company official said.

"When it is ready, the 11th plant will boost the firm's (annual) capacity to 15.8 million tonnes," president director Sudwikatmono told reporters after witnessing the laying of the first foundations of the plant at the firm's complex near Bogor.
The plant is expected to start commercial production by the beginning of 1999 with an annual production capacity of 2.5 million tonnes, he said.

Indocement has said that after its current $800 million expansion programme it expects to boost its annual production capacity to 15.8 million tonnes by the year 1999 from its current capacity of around 9.7 million tonnes.
The expansion programme includes building new plants in Kalimantan as well as Cirebon and Citereup, both in West Java.
Indocement said in a statement on Friday that Japan's Marubeni Corporation and Kawasaki Heavy Industries would jointly build the new plant.
The statement said the plant's cooling equipment would be supplied by F.L. Smidth of Denmark and its mill by Krupp Polysius from Germany.
It said the development of the $230 million plant would be partly financed by the Export Import Bank of Japan as well as the firm's internal funds and other loans.
